title: Learner 01 | Day 053: Migrations and backward compatibility
body:
## Goal

Add an optional session note, backfill a default, and rehearse upgrade and downgrade on sample data.

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/core/operations/session_database.py`

**Method/unit:** `apply_session_note`

**Why here:** This is a domain/application decision: it expresses the calculation or use-case behavior while depending on values and small collaborator contracts.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** Old records remain readable; new records work; downgrade loss is documented before execution.

**Boundaries:** Apply the rule once; use accepted values, not transport parsing or printing.

## Research hints

1. Research **Migrations and backward compatibility**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:docs.sqlalchemy.org Migrations and backward compatibility`; use [SQLAlchemy tutorial](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/tutorial/) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** Why separate calculation from input and printing?

**Review with @praadeep28101995:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.
